The people promised faithfully to obey him.

arxiv-2106-12664.creator: Jonathan S. Gómez, N. D. Padilla, J. C. Helly, C. G. Lacey, C. M. Baugh, C. D. P. Lagos
arxiv-2106-12664.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jonathan S. Gómez, N. D. Padilla, J. C. Helly, C. G. Lacey, C. M. Baugh, C. D. P. Lagos. We examine the effect of using different halo finders and merger tree building algorithms on galaxy properties predicted using the GALFORM semi-analytical model run on a high resolution, large volume dark matter simulation.

arxiv-2107-04257.title: Demonstration of diamond nuclear spin gyroscope
arxiv-2107-04257.creator: A. Jarmola, S. Lourette, V. M. Acosta, A. G. Birdwell, P. Blümler, D. Budker, T. Ivanov, V. S. Malinovsky
arxiv-2107-04257.description: Abstract We demonstrate operation of a rotation sensor based on the 14 N nuclear spins intrinsic to nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond. The sensor employs optical polarization and readout of the nuclei and a radio-frequency double-quantum pulse protocol that monitors 14 N nuclear spin precession.

arxiv-2404-19587.title: Single-Atom Substituents in Copper Surfaces May Adsorb Multiple CO Molecules
arxiv-2404-19587.creator: Magnus A. H. Christiansen, Alejandro Peña-Torres, Elvar Ö. Jónsson, Hannes Jónsson
arxiv-2404-19587.description: Abstract Copper is a good CO 2 electroreduction catalyst as products beyond CO form, but efficiency and selectivity is low. Experiments have shown that an admixture of other elements can help, and computational screening studies have pointed out various promising candidates based on the adsorption of a single CO molecule as a descriptor.

arxiv-2408-12704.title: A General Framework for Gradient-Based Optimization of Superconducting Quantum Circuits using Qubit Discovery as a Case Study
arxiv-2408-12704.creator: Taha Rajabzadeh, Alex Boulton-McKeehan*, Sam Bonkowsky*, David I. Schuster, Amir H. Safavi-Naeini
arxiv-2408-12704.description: Abstract Engineering the Hamiltonian of a quantum system is fundamental to achieving novel goals or better performance. Automating Hamiltonian design through gradient-based optimization can dramatically accelerate this process. However, computing the gradients of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Hamiltonian—a large, sparse matrix—with respect to system properties poses a significant challenge, especially for arbitrary systems.

arxiv-2412-01132.title: Eyes on the Road : State-of-the-Art Video Question Answering Models Assessment for Traffic Monitoring Tasks
arxiv-2412-01132.creator: Joseph Raj Vishal, Divesh Basina, Aarya Choudhary, Bharatesh Chakravarthi
arxiv-2412-01132.description: Abstract Recent advances in the video question answering domain offer promising applications across various fields, particularly in traffic monitoring, where the accurate and efficient interpretation of video data is vital. Within intelligent transportation systems, the ability to answer complex, real-time queries such as “How many red cars passed in the last 10 minutes?

arxiv-2502-16031.title: The applications of Bieri-Neumann-Strebel invariant on Kähler groups
arxiv-2502-16031.creator: Yuan Liu
arxiv-2502-16031.description: Abstract Résumé We give several applications of the Bieri-Neumann-Strebel invariant on Kähler groups. Specifically, we provide simpler proof of the Napier-Ramachandran theorem on the HNN extension about Kähler groups and show that amenable Kähler groups have an empty complement of the BNS invariant.

arxiv-2502-17739.title: Are GNNs doomed by the topology of their input graph?
arxiv-2502-17739.creator: Amine Mohamed Aboussalah, Abdessalam Ed-dib
arxiv-2502-17739.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Amine Mohamed Aboussalah, Abdessalam Ed-dib. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in learning from graph-structured data. However, the influence of the input graph’s topology on GNN behavior remains poorly understood. In this work, we explore whether GNNs are inherently limited by the structure of their input graphs, focusing on how local topological features interact with the message-passing scheme to produce global phenomena such as oversmoothing or expressive representations.

arxiv-2505-19442.title: Style2Code: A Dual-Modal Contrastive Learning Framework for Style-Controllable Code Generation
arxiv-2505-19442.creator: Dutao Zhang, YuLong He, Nicolas Rafael Arroyo Arias, Boyi Li, Kovalchuk
arxiv-2505-19442.description: Abstract Controllable code generation aims to produce source code that adheres to specified style patterns while maintaining functional correctness. This research direction primarily serves scenarios where programmers use code generation models in daily practice, enabling models to better adapt to users’ specific project requirements.

britannica-1911-champion.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-champion.description: Article 'Champion' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 5), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. The office of “king’s champion” (campio regis) is peculiar to England. The function of the king’s champion, when the ceremonial of the coronation was carried out in its completeness, was to ride, clad in complete armour, on his right the high constable, on his left the earl marshal, into Westminster Hall during the coronation banquet, and challenge to single combat any who should dispute the king’s right to reign.

pmc-10565240.title: Barriers to adherence to home-based pulmonary rehabilitation among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in Iran: a descriptive qualitative study
pmc-10565240.creator: Ramin Sami, Kobra Salehi, Marzieh Hashemi, Shila Haghighat, Vajihe Atashi
pmc-10565240.description: ObjectivesChronic obstructive pulmonary disease is a chronic disease with numerous complications. Therefore, its effective management depends on home-based pulmonary rehabilitation. The effectiveness of home-based pulmonary rehabilitation programmes in turn depends on patient adherence to them. The aim of this study was to explore the barriers to adherence to home-based pulmonary rehabilitation among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.DesignQualitative descriptive design.

pmc-10649805.title: CONAN—Novel Tool to Create and Analyze Liquids in Confined Space
pmc-10649805.creator: Leonard Dick, Barbara Kirchner
pmc-10649805.description: Modeling of complex liquids at solid surfaces and in confinement is gaining attention due to an increase in computer power and advancement of simulation techniques. Therefore, tools to set up structures and for analysis are needed. In this paper, we present CONAN—a Python code designed to facilitate the study of liquids interacting with solid structures, such as walls or pores.

pmc-10667856.title: In Situ Forming of Nitric Oxide and Electric Stimulus for Nerve Therapy by Wireless Chargeable Gold Yarn‐Dynamos
pmc-10667856.creator: Min‐Ren Chiang, Ya‐Hui Lin, Wei‐Jie Zhao, Hsiu‐Ching Liu, Ru‐Siou Hsu, Tsu‐Chin Chou, Tsai‐Te Lu, I‐Chi Lee, Lun‐De Liao, Shih‐Hwa Chiou, Li‐An Chu, Shang‐Hsiu Hu
pmc-10667856.description: Endogenous signals, namely nitric oxide (NO) and electrons, play a crucial role in regulating cell fate as well as the vascular and neuronal systems. Unfortunately, utilizing NO and electrical stimulation in clinical settings can be challenging due to NO's short half‐life and the invasive electrodes required for electrical stimulation.

pmc-11346547.title: From both sides of the needle: Understanding effective interventions for facilitating non-national immunization program vaccine decision making in China
pmc-11346547.creator: Mingzhu Jiang, Xuanxuan Yan, Weixi Jiang, Haifeng Ma, Sijuan Zhou, Xiaohua Ying
pmc-11346547.description: Vaccination decisions are influenced by various psychological and practical factors. In China, non-National Immunization Program (non-NIP) vaccines, which are voluntary and self-paid, add uncertainty and autonomy to the decision-making process. Effective communication between providers and recipients is crucial but understudied. This study aims to integrate their perspectives, identify strategies for facilitating vaccination decisions, and analyze their mechanisms.

pmc-11527720.title: Succeed to culture a novel lineage symbiotic bacterium of Mollicutes which widely found in arthropods intestine uncovers the potential double-edged sword ecological function
pmc-11527720.creator: Lingyu Zhang, Qi Chen, Shenzheng Zeng, Zhixuan Deng, Zhongcheng Liu, Xuanting Li, Qilu Hou, Renjun Zhou, Shicheng Bao, Dongwei Hou, Shaoping Weng, Jianguo He, Zhijian Huang
pmc-11527720.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Symbiotic gut bacteria play crucial role in host health. Symbionts are widely distributed in arthropod intestines, but their ecological functions are poorly understood due to the inability to cultivate them. Members of Candidatus Bacilliplasma (CB) are widely distributed in crustacean intestine and maybe commensals with hosts, but the paucity of pure cultures has limited further insights into their physiologies and functions.

pmc-12524546.title: Health Information Seeking and Behavior in the Korean Population During the COVID-19 Pandemic
pmc-12524546.creator: Hanna Choi, Meiling Jin, Byungsun Park, Daniele Giansanti, Joaquim Carreras
pmc-12524546.description: Background: Online health information seeking emerged as a critical form of public health behavior during the COVID-19 pandemic, generating substantial research interest. However, empirical studies examining health information-seeking patterns among Korean populations and their behavioral outcomes during the pandemic remain limited.

pmc-12530381.title: Strategies employed by Iranian nurses for managing workplace bullying: a qualitative descriptive study
pmc-12530381.creator: Saeedeh Piri, Rostam Jalali, Alireza Khatony
pmc-12530381.description: AbstractObjectivesThis study aimed to explore the strategies employed by nurses to manage workplace bullying.DesignQualitative descriptive study.SettingThe study was conducted in a hospital located in western Iran between 21 March and 22 September 2023.ParticipantsA purposive sample of 14 nurses was selected.MethodsData collection was conducted through semistructured in-depth interviews. The collected data were analysed using a conventional content analysis approach.

pmc-12668688.title: A novel predictor of persistent ocular hypotony after pars plana vitrectomy for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment: The initial intraocular pressure difference between the eye with RRD and the fellow eye
pmc-12668688.creator: Ecem Önder Tokuç, V. Levent Karabaş, Sevim Ayça Seyyar, Ece Başaran Emengen, Ahmet Burak Güray, Kübra Atay Dinçer, Ceren Deniz Önder, Emrah Gökay Özgür
pmc-12668688.description: PurposeTo evaluate the predictive value of initial intraocular pressure difference of the detached and fellow eyes of patients with complex rhegmatogenous retinal detachment on postoperative persistent ocular hypotony.MethodsThis retrospective observational study included 538 eyes of 538 unilateral complex rhegmatogenous retinal detachment patients with a proliferative vitreoretinopathy grade of C-1 or higher, treated with silicone oil endotamponade following pars plana vitrectomy.

pmc-12786005.title: Metronomic 5-Fluorouracil and Vinorelbine Reduce Cancer Stemness and Modulate EZH2/NOTCH-1/STAT3 Signaling in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Spheroids
pmc-12786005.creator: Alice Ilari, Emanuela Grassilli, Mario Mauri, Marina E. Cazzaniga, Serena Capici, Marialuisa Lavitrano, Maria Grazia Cerrito
pmc-12786005.description: Triple Negative Breast Cancers (TNBCs) are heterogeneous and aggressive tumors with a median overall survival of less than two years. Despite the availability of new drugs, the prognosis remains poor, implicating a more aggressive clinical course in the metastatic setting.

pmc-13178546.title: Polyolefin blends with co-continuous architectures enabled by dynamic covalent crosslinking
pmc-13178546.creator: Eliza K. Neidhart, Stephanie M. Ribet, Taehyun A. Lee, Logan Kearney, Karen C. Bustillo, Eric A. Dailing, Mutian Hua, Colin Ophus, Sophia N. Fricke, Ah-Young Song, Jeffrey A. Reimer, Erik J. Alexanian, Joanna M. Atkin, Brett A. Helms, Frank A. Leibfarth
pmc-13178546.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Blending polymers produces brittle materials due to macrophase separation and poor interfacial adhesion, which is exemplified by mixtures of polyolefins. This presents a formidable challenge for the mechanical recycling of mixed plastic waste. Here, we demonstrate that dynamic covalent crosslinking of immiscible polyolefin blends creates macrophase separated co-continuous architectures, yet they display excellent mechanical properties, which challenges the conventional wisdom regarding morphology-property relationships in polymer blend compatibilization.

pmc-13217113.title: Between stings and smoke: prevalence of allergic disorders and exposure to combustion smokes in Northeast Italy’s beekeepers
pmc-13217113.creator: Marcella Mauro, Alice Tassinari, Federico Cavallo Ronchi, Marco Rizzo, Francesca Larese Filon
pmc-13217113.description: ObjectivesBeekeepers are frequently exposed to bee venom and combustion smoke, leading to risks of systemic allergic reactions and respiratory hazards. This study assesses the prevalence of systemic allergic symptoms among beekeepers in Northeastern Italy and describes current management practices. Additionally, it characterises inhalation exposures to combustion smoke during apiary maintenance.

pmc-13233010.title: Dermatologic Conditions and Incident Anxiety in Young Adults: Propensity Score–Matched Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13233010.creator: Isabella Zai, Adrian Zai

pmc-13253474.creator: Martina Arcieri, Sandro Pignata, Domenica Lorusso, Anna Fagotti, Vito Chiantera, Antonino Ditto, Giorgio Valabrega, Claudia Marchetti, Claudio Zamagni, Valentina Tuninetti, Alberto Farolfi, Stefano Restaino, Giuseppe Vizzielli

Eight leading Italian experts (four surgeons and four medical oncologists) engaged in a structured debate attended by more than 150 participants.

pmc-13407770.title: Assessing the utility of advanced adoption models for AI-based financial services: insights into automated and hybrid robo-advisors
pmc-13407770.creator: Balraj Verma, Laxmi Remer, Divya Goswami, Somesh Kumar Sinha
pmc-13407770.description: IntroductionFinancial robo-advisors (FRAs), based on artificial intelligence (AI), are changing the ways people make investment decisions by providing advisory services that are based on algorithms and have different degrees of automation. But little evidence exists on the appropriateness of existing technology adoption theories to explain investor adoption of such systems.

pmc-13575202.title: Reinforcement learning-guided multi-objective trajectory planning for obstacle avoidance in robotic manipulators
pmc-13575202.creator: Zhenlong Zhao, Shuang Hao, Bin Jin, Lei Liu, Zhongfeng Li
pmc-13575202.description: Robotic manipulators operating in cluttered environments require collision-free trajectories that remain executable under kinematic and dynamic constraints. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning (RL)-guided multi-objective trajectory planning framework, termed RL-MOP-HNE, for a 6-DOF UR5 manipulator. The planning model simultaneously minimizes path length, energy consumption, and execution time while satisfying collision-avoidance, kinematic, and dynamic constraints.

pmc-13628731.title: Land use types and elevation gradients jointly influence soil bacterial community diversity and functions in the Gaoligong Mountains
pmc-13628731.creator: Ruilong Huang, Wei Li
pmc-13628731.description: Land use types and elevation gradients are key determinants of soil environment, thereby shaping the composition and diversity of soil bacterial communities. Nevertheless, our understanding of how the composition, diversity, and functions of soil bacterial communities vary among land use types along elevation gradients remains limited.
